newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian opposition leader wins parliament seat.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian opposition leader wins parliament seat.

text.p: Ivory Coast's main opposition leader Laurent Gbagbo finally won a seat in the West African nation's second multi-party parliament on Monday -- over one year after the rest of the assembly was elected.

Gbagbo, who spearheaded the 1990 campaign for multi-party politics, was among five members of his Ivorian Popular Front Party who won seats in Sunday by-elections in and around their centre west Gagnoa stronghold, the Interior Ministry said.
President Henri Konan Bedie's Democratic Party (PDCI), which won a crushing victory in the November 1995 parliamentary elections, extended its majority by winning the three other seats at stake.

Gbagbo's 74.3 percent victory in the Ouragahio constituency he won in 1990 followed postponement by the government of the November 1995 poll in the Gagnoa area after political and ethnic clashes killed 25 people there.

Gbagbo and his main opposition allies, Rally of the Republicans dissidents from the ruling party, boycotted the October 1995 presidential poll, triggering political violence in which 35 people died nationwide.

Around Gagnoa, the unrest took an ethnic turn with indigenous Bete supporters of Gbagbo clashing with migrant farmers from Bedie's Baoule tribe. The clashes killed 25 people, mostly Baoules, and sparked a Baoule exodus.

The ethnic rivalry did not spread further in the former French colony, traditionally a model of stability in a turbulent region. Sunday's polling passed off peacefully but under tight security in the Gagnoa area.
Bedie's party now has 149 of the assembly's 175 seats and Gbagbo's party and its RDR allies 13 each.

Ivory Coast, the world's top cocoa producer, held its first multi-party elections in 1990 after independence president Felix Houphouet-Boigny bowed to pressure for reform. Bedie succeeded him on his death in 1993 and won the 1995 presidential poll.

On Sunday, ruling party candidates won in by-elections in Seguela and Korhogo in the north and Adzope in the east. The ruling party won control of three of four town halls at stake. Gbagbo's party won control of the fourth.
Turnout was around 50 percent, the ministry said.
